note: Metronome v2, UA cohort: synchronized re-download loop against the seven pre-existing UA listings' 0.7.3 reuploads, onset 2026-09-06 (the eu-maps 0.7.3 release day), ~6.8/day per listing in fixed slots regardless of listing popularity (zaporizhzhia/kryvyi-rih at 1.0-1.1/day organic run the same weekly totals as kharkiv/lviv/odesa at ~2/day; kyiv = the same uniform floor plus its own ~6/day organic, matching its v0.1.0-era rate). New-version traffic is modeled as loop-inflated ADOPTION releases: legitimate traffic = organic update adoption of the prior install base plus new organic demand, estimated from three clean yukina pack-refresh adoption curves (brno 0.4.1, asahikawa 0.2.2, bydgoszcz-torun 0.5.0 - max-fraction pooling errs toward attributing less). Retired/superseded versions are not targeted. CAP: daily_spurious_cap=7 is the measured uniform loop rate per listing (maintainer ruling 2026-10-03, #12201; hourly lockstep slots measure ~7.5-8/day outside release-day waves, so 7 errs toward attributing less). It was first applied by an uncommitted script that left the ledger timeline uncapped; repaired by scripts/ops/repair-metronome-ua-cap-consistency.ts, and the cap now lives here so every re-apply (including after an attribution-ledger rebuild) is capped natively. 0.8.1 EXTENSION (2026-10-07): eu-maps 0.8.1 (published 2026-10-04T21:56Z) did NOT stop the client - after a ~29h pause it resumed 2026-10-05T06Z on the new versions and now hits all 22 UA listings in lockstep (the fifteen 0.7.3-cohort listings first joined on their first update, 0.1.0 -> 0.1.1). 0.2.1 x7 and 0.1.1 x15 added as adoption targets from their first counted snapshot (2026-10-06); they measure their install base net of attribution (install_base=adjusted - raw would count the ~185 loop fetches each 0.2.0 carries as installs and widen the very allowance meant to remove them); the 0.2.0 targets end at 2026-10-04 (target incident_end), the last snapshot day carrying 0.2.0 loop slots - later 0.2.0 traffic is organic stragglers on a superseded version. The client follows the update manifest, so a release cannot kill it; incident_end stays open. RIDERS (2026-10-25): listings the same client re-fetches in the UA loop's hours (detect-metronome; reviewed in KNOWN_INCIDENTS.md) are corrected by rider_targets on the loop's own clock (per_cycle x the seven originals' lockstep hours per snapshot day, capped by the version's raw growth). Riders join when the client updates them and drop out when it restarts (2026-10-04); open windows are re-applied daily by the metronome guard.
